extracted.intended_audience: clinical trial investigators and protocol authors (also useful to sponsors, funders, ethics committees/IRBs, peer reviewers, journals, registries, and regulators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for the minimum content to include when drafting protocols for interventional clinical trials, intended to improve completeness, transparency, and facilitate appraisal, conduct, and reporting of trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title (1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptive title identifying the study design, population, interventions, and, if applicable, trial acronym
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, descriptive title that communicates key trial features (design, population, interventions). Aids identification and indexing of the protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial registration — trial identifier and registry name (2a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial identifier and registry name. If not yet registered, name of intended registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the registry and identifier (or intended registry) so the trial can be located in registries; registration promotes transparency and reduces selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial registration — WHO Trial Registration Data Set items (2b)
rubrics_metrics.description: All items from the World Health Organization Trial Registration Data Set (Appendix Table, available at www.annals.org).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure protocol contains or references the full WHO-required registration data elements to standardize essential trial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol version (3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Date and version identifier
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record versioning so readers and oversight bodies can track amendments; include dates and identifiers for auditability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding (4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources and types of financial, material, and other support
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose all funding and material support to allow assessment of potential conflicts of interest and resource adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities — protocol contributors (5a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names, affiliations, and roles of protocol contributors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List contributors and their roles to clarify responsibility for protocol components and authorship; supports accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities — sponsor contact (5b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Name and contact information for the trial sponsor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sponsor contact details for administrative, governance, and regulatory communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities — sponsor and funder roles (5c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of study sponsor and funders, if any, in study design; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of data; writing of the report; and the decision to submit the report for publication, including whether they will have ultimate authority over any of these activities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the degree of sponsor/funder involvement in scientific and publication-related decisions to disclose potential influence and protect research integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities — oversight composition (5d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition, roles, and responsibilities of the coordinating center, steering committee, end point adjudication committee, data management team, and other individuals or groups overseeing the trial, if applicable (see item 21a for DMC)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail governance structures and responsibilities; reference charters where appropriate to clarify decision-making and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and rationale — research question & justification (6a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of research question and justification for undertaking the trial, including summary of relevant studies (published and unpublished) examining benefits and harms for each intervention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context and evidence base that justify the trial; include both published and unpublished evidence relevant to benefits and harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and rationale — choice of comparators (6b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation for choice of comparators
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why selected comparators are appropriate (e.g., standard care, placebo) to support interpretation of effect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific objectives or hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State primary and key secondary objectives/hypotheses clearly to drive outcome selection, sample size, and analysis plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial design (8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of trial design, including type of trial (e.g., parallel group, crossover, factorial, single group), allocation ratio, and framework (e.g., superiority, equivalence, noninferiority, exploratory)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify design features and trial framework to inform methods, sample size, and analytic approach; be explicit about allocation ratios and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study setting (9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of study settings (e.g., community clinic, academic hospital) and list of countries where data will be collected. Reference to where list of study sites can be obtained
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe settings and geographic scope to inform generalizability; reference detailed site lists if numerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria (10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion and exclusion criteria for participants. If applicable, eligibility criteria for study centers and individuals who will perform the interventions (e.g., surgeons, psychotherapists)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define participant and provider/site eligibility clearly to enable reproducibility and assessment of external validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions — description for replication (11a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interventions for each group with sufficient detail to allow replication, including how and when they will be administered
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough procedural and dosing detail so another team could implement the same interventions; include timing and administration procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions — discontinuation or modification criteria (11b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for discontinuing or modifying allocated interventions for a given trial participant (e.g., drug dose change in response to harms, participant request, or improving/worsening disease)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify stopping/modification rules for safety or efficacy reasons to guide consistent in-trial decision-making and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions — adherence strategies and monitoring (11c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies to improve adherence to intervention protocols, and any procedures for monitoring adherence (e.g., drug tablet return, laboratory tests)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe methods to promote and measure adherence to assess intervention fidelity and interpret outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions — relevant concomitant care (11d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant concomitant care and interventions that are permitted or prohibited during the trial
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List allowed/prohibited concomitant treatments to avoid confounding and clarify participant management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes (12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary, secondary, and other outcomes, including the specific measurement variable (e.g., systolic blood pressure), analysis metric (e.g., change from baseline, final value, time to event), method of aggregation (e.g., median, proportion), and time point for each outcome. Explanation of the clinical relevance of chosen efficacy and harm outcomes is strongly recommended
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define each outcome precisely (variable, metric, aggregation, time point) and justify clinical relevance; detailed definitions reduce risk of selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant timeline (13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time schedule of enrollment, interventions (including any run-ins and washouts), assessments, and visits for participants. A schematic diagram is highly recommended (Figure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a schedule and preferably a schematic diagram to clarify participant flow, assessments, and timing of procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size (14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated number of participants needed to achieve study objectives and how it was determined, including clinical and statistical assumptions supporting any sample size calculations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report assumptions, effect sizes, power, alpha, and other inputs; justify clinically meaningful effect sizes and any adjustments for attrition or multiplicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment (15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies for achieving adequate participant enrollment to reach target sample size
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe recruitment approaches, anticipated rates, and contingency plans to meet enrollment targets and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation sequence generation (16a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method of generating the allocation sequence (e.g., computer-generated random numbers), and list of any factors for stratification. To reduce predictability of a random sequence, details of any planned restriction (e.g., blocking) should be provided in a separate document that is unavailable to those who enroll participants or assign interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify randomisation methods, stratification factors, and any restrictions; protect concealment by keeping detailed restriction info unavailable to enrollers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation concealment mechanism (16b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism of implementing the allocation sequence (e.g., central telephone; sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes), describing any steps to conceal the sequence until interventions are assigned
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe practical mechanisms to ensure allocation concealment to prevent selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation — who does what in allocation (16c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who will generate the allocation sequence, who will enroll participants, and who will assign participants to interventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify roles in the randomization process to ensure separation of duties and reduce risk of manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding (masking) — who is blinded and how (17a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who will be blinded after assignment to interventions (e.g., trial participants, care providers, outcome assessors, data analysts), and how
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which parties are blinded and the methods used; acknowledge feasibility limits and describe measures to minimize bias if blinding is not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding — unblinding circumstances and procedure (17b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If blinded, circumstances under which unblinding is permissible, and procedure for revealing a participant’s allocated intervention during the trial
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify criteria and procedures for unblinding for safety or other reasons and who has authority to unblind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection methods — assessment and data quality (18a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for assessment and collection of outcome, baseline, and other trial data, including any related processes to promote data quality (e.g., duplicate measurements, training of assessors) and a description of study instruments (e.g., questionnaires, laboratory tests) along with their reliability and validity, if known. Reference to where data collection forms can be found, if not in the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe instruments, measurement procedures, training, and quality assurance to ensure valid and reliable data; reference forms and validation evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection methods — retention and follow-up (18b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans to promote participant retention and complete follow-up, including list of any outcome data to be collected for participants who discontinue or deviate from intervention protocols
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include retention strategies and specify which data will still be collected from dropouts to support intention-to-treat analyses and minimize attrition bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management (19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for data entry, coding, security, and storage, including any related processes to promote data quality (e.g., double data entry; range checks for data values). Reference to where details of data management procedures can be found, if not in the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document data handling procedures, security measures, quality checks, and locations of detailed SOPs or manuals to ensure integrity and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods — primary and secondary analyses (20a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical methods for analyzing primary and secondary outcomes. Reference to where other details of the statistical analysis plan can be found, if not in the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide main analytic methods, modeling approaches, and references to a full statistical analysis plan; be specific about hypothesis tests and estimation techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods — additional analyses (20b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for any additional analyses (e.g., subgroup and adjusted analyses)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify planned subgroup, interaction, and adjusted analyses (including rationale) to reduce data-driven post hoc analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods — analysis population & missing data (20c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of analysis population relating to protocol nonadherence (e.g., as-randomized analysis), and any statistical methods to handle missing data (e.g., multiple imputation)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define primary analysis population (e.g., intention-to-treat, per-protocol) and missing data strategies to ensure transparency in handling deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data monitoring — DMC composition and role (21a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of DMC; summary of its role and reporting structure; statement of whether it is independent from the sponsor and competing interests; and reference to where further details about its charter can be found, if not in the protocol. Alternatively, an explanation of why a DMC is not needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the Data Monitoring Committee, independence, and charter; if no DMC, justify why one is unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data monitoring — interim analyses and stopping guidelines (21b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of any interim analyses and stopping guidelines, including who will have access to these interim results and make the final decision to terminate the trial
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify planned interim looks, stopping rules, and governance for decision-making to avoid ad hoc stopping and preserve trial integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harms (22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for collecting, assessing, reporting, and managing solicited and spontaneously reported adverse events and other unintended effects of trial interventions or trial conduct
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define adverse event reporting procedures, assessment, and management, including timelines and responsible parties, to protect participant safety and meet regulatory expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditing (23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency and procedures for auditing trial conduct, if any, and whether the process will be independent from investigators and the sponsor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe auditing plans and independence to ensure compliance with protocol and applicable regulations; reference audit charters or SOPs where available.
